# PR Preparation Skill

## Purpose
Assemble a concise, review-ready pull-request package for the completed Book API documentation-sync change.

## When to use
Use after requirements, architecture, design review, implementation, code review, and verification are complete.

## Responsibilities
- Summarize the implemented change and its narrow scope.
- Map the change to the user story and acceptance criteria.
- Include verified test evidence and documented limitations.
- Confirm review and verification stages are complete.
- Identify reviewer-relevant risks, especially documentation preservation.

## Inputs
- Final implementation summary and diff.
- Requirements, review outcomes, and verification evidence.
- Approved changelog or validation artifacts.

## Expected outputs
- A concise PR title and body or review package.
- Accurate change summary, test evidence, acceptance-criteria status, and known limitations.
- A reviewer checklist showing completed SDLC stages.

## Constraints
- Do not create or submit a PR unless explicitly authorized by the workflow owner.
- Do not claim validation or review work that lacks evidence.
- Do not add unrelated scope, new features, or undocumented limitations.
- Keep the package limited to the Book API GET /books/{id} documentation-sync change.
